title: What To Do If There's a Risk of Lightning
question: If you think there is a risk of lightning nearby while you are playing, what should you do according to the Rules of Golf?

choices.text: Keep playing until the Committee officially suspends play
Wait for your friends to decide
Stop playing immediately for your own safety
Only stop playing if it starts to rain

explanation: If you believe there is a danger from lightning, you should stop play at once, even if the Committee has not yet officially suspended play.

juniorVersion.title: What Should You Do If There’s Lightning Nearby?
juniorVersion.question: You hear thunder or see lightning while playing golf. What should you do?

choices.text: Keep playing until someone who runs the game tells you to stop
Let your friends decide what to do
Stop playing right away to stay safe
Only stop playing if it starts to rain

juniorVersion.explanation: If you see lightning or hear thunder, you must stop playing golf straight away, even if the main people in charge haven’t told everyone to stop yet. This keeps you safe.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A bright flash of electricity during a storm. It can be very dangerous.
The group of people in charge of the golf competition or course.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind children that safety always comes first. Practise what to do if there’s a thunderstorm before you go out to play.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think it’s OK to keep playing if the Committee hasn’t told them to stop.
Some might wait for rain or for others to choose.
